summary: Eleven experiments completed in 4.2 minutes, including five compute-bound tasks. The longest listed compute-bound entries were the 3.27-minute semantic-parity-gated flagship ASP benchmark, the 0.73-minute ARC mechanic-class router, and the 0.12-minute post-marker source freeze. The timing data does not isolate why they took those durations.
bottlenecks_identified: The semantic-parity-gated flagship ASP benchmark was the main recorded compute bottleneck at 3.27 minutes; no phase data explains the duration.
Disk-modification-time reconstruction ranks the experiments but does not separate gate wait, model load, inference, or teardown time.
The GPU state is not linked to experiment intervals, and no loaded-model-count or runner-selection receipt is available. GPU efficiency and concurrent-model routing therefore cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic start and stop times for each experiment and each execution phase instead of relying on disk modification times.
Attach GPU utilization samples, process identity, and workload type to every compute-bound experiment interval.
Record loaded-model count and runner selection, and select DualGPURunner only when multiple models run in parallel.
Time readiness-gate checks separately from benchmark execution so the semantic-parity-gated path has an actionable breakdown.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add one task-correlated execution receipt with phase timing, GPU samples, process identity, model count, and runner choice.
Replace disk-modification-time reconstruction with monotonic experiment and phase timers.
Add a compute-task GPU engagement check and preserve single-GPU dispatch for single-model work.
meta_reflection: Disk-modification-time reconstruction can rank entries but cannot explain them. The next retrospective should distinguish measured bottlenecks from telemetry gaps and should not infer GPU or runner defects without task-correlated receipts.
